scenario: AITA for expecting family time? | This morning I woke up and saw my husband watching video game streams, his typical pastime. Later he said the streamers he was watching were having cash giveaways that required participation to be entered. He continued to watch while he covertly built the kids' bikes in the garage as I had asked, then left to run a last-minute grocery errand for dinner, then came home and went upstairs to watch more streaming. After wrapping gifts, I did dishes and put dinner in the oven, and asked him to turn it off to spend time with me with/without kids. He said no. That the stream was only for today and it is not okay for me to expect him to stop doing what he finds enjoyable just because I want him to do something I find enjoyable. But if I was okay letting him spend $100 on app purchases for this game (same one he's watching) that he'd shut it off no problem. But last year he spent a little over $2,000 on in-app purchases for this game, and after a lengthy discussion, said he wouldn't buy anymore. So I'm not a huge fan of okaying any more money for it. It's almost 6pm and says he doesn't know when it will end, but that there are 2 more streamers left. I feel like the evening is almost over and I am so disappointed and feel saddened that he would rather watch games than spend time with me. Am I an asshole for being upset and having unrealistic expectations?

First, I need to understand the scenario properly. The husband was watching video game streams, which included cash giveaways that required participation. He was also building the kids' bikes as asked, then went grocery shopping, came back, and continued watching streams. When the wife asked him to stop to spend time with her, he refused, saying it's not okay for her to expect him to stop his enjoyable activity just because she wants something else. He also mentioned that if she okayed $100 for app purchases, he'd stop, but she's not happy about that because he spent $2000 last year and promised not to buy more.

So the main issue here is whether the wife's expectation for family time is reasonable. The husband is prioritizing his streaming over family time, even though he did some tasks (building bikes, grocery shopping). But he's continuing to stream when she wants to spend time together.

Now, moral acceptability. The key points here are mutual respect, communication, and balancing individual interests with family time. In a relationship, both partners should have time for their own interests, but also quality time together. The husband's refusal to stop streaming when asked for family time might be seen as dismissive of his wife's needs. However, he's also doing some chores and has a hobby. But the fact that he spent a lot on in-app purchases before and promised not to, but now is still engaging with the game (even if not buying, just watching streams), might indicate a pattern.

But the question is about the wife's action: expecting family time and being upset. Is that morally acceptable? Well, expecting to spend time with your spouse in the evening is reasonable. It's part of maintaining a healthy relationship. If the husband is consistently prioritizing his hobbies over family time, that's a problem. But the wife's expectation itself isn't wrong. She's not asking him to stop all hobbies, just to spend time together when she's made the effort to prepare dinner, wrap gifts, etc.

The husband's argument that "it's not okay for me to expect him to stop doing what he finds enjoyable just because I want him to do something I find enjoyable" is a bit of a false equivalence. Because family time isn't just "something she finds enjoyable"—it's a shared responsibility in a relationship. Both partners should contribute to quality time. If he's watching streams for hours while she's doing household tasks, that's not balanced.

Also, the fact that he's willing to stop if she spends money on the game shows he's prioritizing the game over her, which is problematic. But the wife's refusal to spend more money on the game is reasonable given past spending. So her not okaying the $100 is justified.
